ut_west_facing_wall_2.blurb: One of two cliffs at the Hideaway, a limestone zone high on the north side of American Fork Canyon. This wall catches the afternoon and evening light and holds 21 bolted sport routes, running from 5.10 to 5.13 with most of the lines in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. The rock is pocketed and varied: the uphill end is a little less than vertical, while the downhill end steepens into overhanging ground finished by a prominent arete. It sits well above the canyon floor and the hike in is long by canyon standards, so expect a committed day rather than a quick lap. A good pick for solid 5.10 and 5.11 climbers who like pockets.

ut_watchtower_the_2.blurb: A limestone crag a few miles up American Fork Canyon, on the road toward the Alpine Loop. All 21 routes are bolted sport lines, spanning roughly 5.10 to 5.13 with the bulk at 5.11 and 5.12. The movement here leans technical, built from edges, crimps and side pulls with the odd jug, a change of pace from the pocket-pulling the canyon is famous for. Climbers describe it as a pleasant, lightly visited spot, and it is a good option when the canyon's steeper walls feel too intense. It suits a relaxed afternoon of working a few mid-grade to hard lines.

ut_hell_cave.blurb: A steep limestone cave in American Fork Canyon, part of the Hell Area and known as the home of some of the hardest sport climbing in Utah. All 21 routes are bolted and graded high: mostly 5.13, a handful at 5.14, and only one below that. This is a place for strong, experienced sport climbers; there is nothing here for beginners or anyone still building up to 5.12. The overhanging rock demands power and finger strength more than endurance. The cave is reached by a short trail that climbs from the road and contours across scree, so the walk in is brief.

ut_beachball_crag.blurb: A small, heavily shaded crag beside the creek in Big Cottonwood Canyon, east of Salt Lake City, just up the road from the Ledgemere picnic area. Of its 21 routes, nearly all are trad, with one sport line and one top-rope. The grades lean easy: a number of climbs fall between 5.3 and 5.8, then a few reach 5.10 and a single route about 5.12. Some lines start right at the water's edge, making it a cool choice for a hot day. The approach takes about a minute and you can walk off either side, and the western end tends to draw families and young climbers learning to place gear.
